public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hyperscalers' capex will exceed their cash flows as of Q3 2026, and their AI returns are poor enough that they don't disclose AI revenues beyond run rates.

statement.excerpt: Hyperscalers — who will see their capex outpace their cashflows as of Q3 2026 — have had such poor returns on their investment in AI that none of them will actually disclose their revenues outside of vague “run rates,” which means that all of this investment is effectively based on the idea that something completely different will happen in the future.

from_speaker: poor returns on their investment in AI
our_interpretation: Hyperscalers means Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta, the companies named immediately before this sentence.

For the spending forecast, the plain reading compares their combined cash capital expenditures with combined operating cash flow during calendar Q3 2026. A company-by-company reading is also plausible.
Cash flow means operating cash flow before capital spending, avoiding a comparison with free cash flow that already subtracts capex.
The nondisclosure and poor-return assertions describe the state at publication. Their target is calendar Q1 2026, the latest ordinary reporting quarter preceding the June 30 post.
The causal assertion requires evidence that poor AI returns explain nondisclosure. Nondisclosure alone cannot establish poor returns.
The post supplies no accounting basis for the crossover comparison.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable Q3 results establish the spending crossover, the historical disclosure review finds no realized AI revenue amounts beyond run rates, and evidence establishes poor AI returns as the reason for that disclosure pattern.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable complete Q3 results show no aggregate crossover; or a qualifying historical realized AI revenue disclosure disproves the universal disclosure assertion; or direct evidence refutes the asserted causal explanation. Any partial finding must be identified separately.
